title: What happens while you wait for a first hospital outpatient appointment in Northern Ireland?
scope: Northern Ireland, first consultant-led outpatient appointments
reader: A patient referred for a first outpatient appointment who wants to know how the queue works, how to check it and what the published waits mean.
primaryAngle: Follow a referral from receipt and clinical prioritisation to confirmation and offer of the first appointment.
secondaryAngle: Compare the age of the open waiting list over time and by trust or specialty, and explain how that differs from how long people who were seen actually waited.
lastingValue: The pathway and public measures answer an ongoing patient question and can be refreshed with each quarterly release.

signals.detail: The Department of Health calendar lists the September 2026 outpatient waiting-list bulletin for 3 December 2026.
The Assembly Committee for Health heard an Elective Care Framework and waiting-list update on 12 November 2026.

evidence.reason: The patient-facing process, returns and comparable snapshots are available from the responsible bodies.

evidenceGap: Quarter-end returns count people still waiting. They leave open the full referral-to-appointment experience and why an individual case stays in the queue.
draftingChecks: Check one additional trust's guidance before generalising the Northern Trust process. Identify which referral event starts each measure, and what people can do if their condition changes or their referral appears missing.

Extract ages from the latest consultant-led bulletin and comparable earlier quarters. Preserve the distinction between first appointment, diagnosis and treatment, and check recording changes before comparing trusts.
Check whether the funding source specifies outputs for first appointments, and follow the committee briefing to any agreed follow-up.
